description.narrative: Detta projekt syftar till att stärka rättvisa, mänskliga rättigheter och demokratisk samhällsstyrning i Etiopien genom att ta itu med strukturella utmaningar och stödja inkluderande, ansvarsfullt och rättighetsbaserat styre. Det svarar på pågående konflikter, krympande samhällsutrymme och avstannade reformer genom ett dubbelt fokus på institutionell reform och samhällsstärkande. Projektet stöder institutionell reform samtidigt som det ger samhällen, särskilt marginaliserade grupper som offer för konfliktrelaterade kränkningar av mänskliga rättigheter, kvinnor, personer med funktionsnedsättning och internflyktingar, möjlighet att hävda sina rättigheter och delta meningsfullt i nationella processer.

This project aims to strengthen justice, human rights, and democratic governance in Ethiopia by addressing structural challenges and supporting inclusive, accountable, rights-based governance. It responds to ongoing conflict, shrinking civic space, and stalled reforms through a dual focus on institutional reform and community empowerment. The project supports institutional reform while empowering communities, particularly marginalized groups such as victims of conflict related human rights abuses, women, people with disabilities, and internally displaced persons, to claim their rights and participate meaningfully in national processes.

•Strengthen the rule of law and accountability for human rights violations in Ethiopia by supporting redress and accountability measures in response to human rights violations and supporting rights-holders accessing justice including through transitional justice.
•Support the integration of human rights and rights-based approaches into peace processes e.g. the implementation of the Cessation of Hostilities Agreement (CoHA), other imminent peace processes in Amhara and Oromia regions and eventual related processes such as DDR impacting conflict prevention and humanitarian response efforts. This through strengthened and systematic human rights and protection monitoring in hotspot locations, early warning, and prevention, through engagement with local authorities and civil society organizations; and the creation of Human Rights Fora at regional level for effective coordination, engagement, risk identification and response to systemic issues. •Address inequalities and discrimination in Ethiopia especially affecting women, persons with disabilities and other specific groups.
•Promote rights-based legislative and institutional reforms that enhance and protect civic space and peoples participation, as well as the rule of law and accountability.
•Strengthen the voices of Ethiopian victims, survivors and other civil society advocates to participate in decision-making processes affecting their lives such as legal reforms and strategically promote their rights.
